title: What is known about 1RB1LB_0RC0LD_1LD1RE_1RC0LA_1RD1RF_0RD---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1LB_0RC0LD_1LD1RE_1RC0LA_1RD1RF_0RD---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The tape is a short word at the left and two big blocks of ones; each round trip moves 3 ones out of one block and 4 into the other, so each regime multiplies the count by about 4/3. Lean proves the 35 one-cycle rules used on the run to 1015 steps; the accelerated run reaches 1040 steps without a halt.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 48,667 cells have been visited and 28,884 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.117). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.517).

claims.title: The cycle rules
claims.text: 35 one-cycle rules, each for all values of its variables, e.g. cycle23: a block of 3-cell words (111)^n1 grows by 8 words while (111)^n3 shrinks by 6, in 36·n3 + 198 steps. They are exactly the rules the cycle accelerator applied on the run to 1015 steps.

claims.title: No halt up to 10<sup>40</sup> steps
claims.text: bbtools.cycles with blocks of 3 cells: 145 jumps, 70 proved rules, no halt by 1040 steps (each jump checked by the proved rule it applies; the steps between are exact macro steps).

claims.title: The 4/3 map
claims.text: The number of cycles per regime goes 3, 7, 12, 17, 25, 36, 49, 67, 89, 117, 159, 218, 290, 385, 511, …, 4498, 6003, 8005, 10672, 14230, 18972, 25273, 33701, 44967: each about 4/3 of the last, with an offset of a few units that depends on the remainder mod 3 and on the word at the left end.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Open. The end-of-regime rule (what the remainder mod 3 does to the left-end word) is not worked out, so the halting condition (F reading 1) is not yet reduced to a statement about the map.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB1RF_1RC0LD_1LB1RA_1RE1LE_0RC0LB_0RB--- up to renaming, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. The same table as 1RB1LC_1LA0RD_1LB1LF_1LE1RE_0LA0RB_0LB--- up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Two big blocks of ones trade cells, four in for every three out, so their size grows by a factor of about 4/3 per round: a Collatz-like map, with a little word at the left end listening to the remainders.

facts.text: No halt in the accelerated (proved-rule) run.
The cycle rules of the run to 10<sup>15</sup>, proved in Lean.
Each regime is about 4/3 as long as the one before.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.117). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.517).
After 109 steps the tape spans 48,667 cells (75 left of the start, 35,199 right), with a density of 1s of 0.594.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: A short word and two big blocks of ones
html: After 109 steps the right part of the tape is 1 0 1^39 0 1^10903 0 1^37419 with the head in D at the right end; the 75 cells left of the start are a short structure of words 100. Each round trip takes 3 ones from the right block and adds 4 to the block before it: at step 60,479 the end of the tape is 1^181 0 1^156, 25 round trips later 1^281 0 1^81. When the right block runs out a new regime starts.

sections.heading: Four in, three out
html: Seen through blocks of 3 cells, a typical cycle (Lean: cycle23) turns (111)^(n1+1) … (111)^(n3+7) into the same tape with n1 + 8 and n3 + 1: 24 cells gained for 18 lost. So when the shrinking block of n cells is used up, the other has grown by about 4n/3, and the next regime is 4/3 as long. The counts of cycles per regime: 3, 7, 12, 17, 25, 36, 49, 67, 89, 117, 159, …, 6003, 8005, 10672, 14230, 18972.

sections.heading: Open
html: The only halting transition is F reading 1. As for other machines of this family, it is decided by how the remainders of the count mod 3 drive the short word at the left end; that end-of-regime rule has not been extracted, so the question is not reduced to a clean map yet. The accelerated run (each jump a proved rule) reaches 1040 steps with no halt.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

summary: Two long blocks of ones on the right trade cells, 4 gained for every 3 lost per round trip, so the run is a Collatz-like map n → about 4n/3 (offset set by n mod 3 and a short left-end word); the halting question is not reduced yet.
